epigraph.quote: Separate the quality of the factory from the price of the stock, and never pay a compounder multiple for a cyclical balance sheet.

web_blocks.text: What Kross Limited Does & Why It Is Under Review

web_blocks.html: Kross Limited (NSE: KROSS) is a Jamshedpur-based Tier-1 maker of safety-critical forged and machined parts for heavy trucks (M&HCVs) and tractors [1][2]. It also builds single-piece extruded trailer axles and suspension units [1][2]. Since entering trailer systems in 2019, Kross grew that unit to 43%–49% of sales [3][4]. Q2 FY27 sales jumped +79.6% YoY to ₹235.1 Cr, and PAT rose +143.5% YoY to ₹19.69 Cr [3][4][11]. Yet its three-year record shows sharp swings, including flat ₹620 Cr FY25 sales [1]. It also carries 124-day working capital (107 debtor days, 105 inventory days), 30.4% three-year CFO/PAT conversion, and -₹111 Cr free cash flow [1][11]. Those cash strains earn a price-blind business rating of CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL (`PASS_WITH_WATCH`) [1][11].

web_blocks.text: Dual Portfolio Verdict, Price Levels & Three-Horizon Judgment

web_blocks.html: On November 13, 2026, Kross closed at ₹305.90 (28.42x TTM P/E, ₹1,970.44 Cr market cap) [23]. The stock sits in a confirmed Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend (`13 weeks`, `+51.06%` 3-month gain) [23]. However, it is extended +16.19% above its 50-DMA (₹263.27) and +12.41% above its 10-week EMA (₹272.14) [23]. Kross has no NSE F&O options chain (`NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID`) [23]. In our Zerodha positions ledger, Kross is held as a 1-share tracking position (cost ₹288.75, market value ₹305.90, +₹17.15 gain, 0.01% weight), so our holding action is HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP (`holding_shares_to_sell = 0`, 1-share stop-loss at ₹212.00). Our new-capital verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (`TIER_3`, `STAGE2_PULLBACK_WATCH`). At ₹305.90, Base Case upside to ₹400.00 (25.0x FY28E fully diluted EPS of ₹16.00 across 6.75 Cr diluted shares) gives only 1.00:1 reward-to-risk against the ₹212.00 stop. A pullback into ₹268.00–₹282.00—paired with Q3 FY27 working capital < 105 days or Feb–Mar 2027 seamless tube trials on track—widens asymmetry to 1.69:1.

web_blocks.takeaway: Kross is an improving operational story trading at an extended short-term price. Patience for ₹268–₹282 turns a 1.00:1 chase into a 1.69:1 asymmetric setup.

web_blocks.html: The tactical takeaway is clear: Kross is a real turnaround story, with Q2 FY27 sales up +79.6% YoY [3]. That jump is already priced into a +51.06% three-month rally to ₹305.90 [23]. Retain the 1-share Zerodha tracking stake with a hard stop at ₹212.00, and for new capital wait for a pullback into ₹268.00–₹282.00 against the ₹212.00 stop. Doing so lifts Base Case reward-to-risk from 1.00:1 to 1.69:1. Keep 100% of marginal cash ready until price and Q3 FY27 working-capital proof align.

Across the three horizons, our rules stay firm. Short-term traders have no F&O edge and face resistance near the ₹326.40 52-week high [23]. Medium-term buyers should demand a pullback to ₹268.00–₹282.00 and watch Q3 FY27 working capital (<105 days). Long-term buyers should wait for positive free cash flow and February–March 2027 seamless tube trials before raising conviction [9][11]. Meanwhile, keeping 100% of the marginal ₹1,00,000 slice in cash protects dry powder against peer options like APL Apollo Tubes and Jamna Auto.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our institutional dossier on Kross Limited. Before you and I spend ten chapters walking through five Jamshedpur manufacturing plants, 124-day working-capital cycles, and multi-timeframe stock charts, let me give you the bottom line up front—and the exact rules that govern it.

Kross Limited is a credible, backward-integrated Tier-1 supplier of forged truck and tractor components and single-piece extruded trailer axles. Its trailer business has scaled to nearly half of revenue, and Q2 FY27 sales jumped 79.6% year over year to ₹235.1 Cr. Yet across FY24–FY26, operating cash flow converted only 30.4% of net profit, free cash flow totaled -₹111 Cr, and borrowings plus an October 2026 preferential issue funded its ₹167 Cr seamless tube plant. That earns a price-blind business verdict of CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL.

In the verified portfolio ledger, Zerodha holds a 1-share tracking position in Kross (cost ₹288.75, market value ₹305.90, +₹17.15 gain, 0.01% weight), which we retain under HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP (0 shares to sell now; 1-share hard stop at ₹212.00). At ₹305.90, the stock is extended 16.19% above its 50-day moving average, offering just 1.00:1 reward-to-risk to our ₹400.00 Base Target (25.0x ₹16.00 FY28E diluted EPS) against the ₹212.00 structural stop. Our new-capital verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_3): keep 100% of your marginal ₹1,00,000 in cash until Kross pulls back into ₹268.00–₹282.00 (1.69:1 asymmetry) and confirms Q3 FY27 working-capital or tube-mill discipline.

book_subsections.title: How to Read This Monograph
paragraphs: Chapters 1 through 6 were written completely price-blind, auditing Kross’s 1991 origins, segment economics, ₹100 revenue waterfall, rivals, management promises, and cash conversion without looking at a single stock quote. Chapters 7 through 9 then capture today’s ₹305.90 price, compare Kross against Jamna Auto, GNA Axles, Ramkrishna Forgings, and Happy Forgings, inspect the Stage 2 chart, and lay out our exact alerts and redeployment plan.

Think of this dossier as two distinct filters working in sequence. The first filter asks whether Kross Limited is a business you want to own over a full industrial cycle: we test its Jamshedpur forging bays, its trailer axle economics, its customer concentration, and its cash conversion before ever glancing at a stock quote. The second filter asks whether today’s market price of ₹305.90 pays you enough for the risks on the balance sheet.

Why does that order matter so much for your portfolio? Because when a stock rallies 51% in three months on an explosive quarterly earnings print, the human temptation is to rationalize away the 124-day working capital cycle and buy at any price. By locking our business rating at CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL first, we keep our feet on the ground—respecting the Q2 FY27 momentum while insisting on a ₹268.00–₹282.00 entry price.

Keep one overarching rule in mind as you read forward: a great factory tour does not automatically make a great stock at any price. Our job is to respect what Kross has built in Jamshedpur—especially its single-piece extruded trailer axles—while refusing to ignore the 124-day working capital cycle or chase a +51% three-month rally.
By the end of Chapter 9, you will have every exact trigger, peer comparison, and cash-redeployment rule needed to act calmly if Kross pulls back into our ₹268.00–₹282.00 entry zone.

Treat this prologue as your map for the entire decision: Kross has real engineering momentum in trailer axles, yet its 124-day working capital cycle and +51.06% three-month rally demand patience for ₹268.00–₹282.00 rather than chasing ₹305.90.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: The Discipline of Waiting
book_callouts.quote: Good companies at stretched prices test your patience; great processes protect your capital until price and fundamentals shake hands.
book_callouts.text: Kross’s Q2 FY27 surge is real, and its ₹212.00 preferential issue floor is well-defined. Retaining our 1-share tracking stake while waiting for ₹268–₹282 for new capital is how you capture the upside without overpaying for execution.
